questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The film courses and the cultural differences. Exploring a new way of studying

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The courses that were available when I signed up for exchange were not available, when I had to choose courses. In the end I only got one film course, which I did really like. The social life was great and the dorms/halls were a good way to make friends.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of mails and also a zoom introduction for us.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Victoria Park Halls

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Catered food and kitchens where you could cook yourself

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
Its pretty nice to live at either Campus or Victoria Park, as Fallowfield is quite far away from the campus
A lot of the people there are pretty young though, as they are first years. It's nice to meet other exchange students this way and eat together.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was easy enough to find the courses, but the system is not that good. Like I said earlier, the courses for exchange students were changed and some what I wanted were deleted. I had to apply three times to get the number of courses that I needed. And I also had to contact a lecturer myself through mail to get the last course.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You apply for the courses you need, then they write which courses you get. Then you apply again until you get the course you want. It was not the smartest system, because you couldn't see how full the courses were.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I had to seek

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: like I said earlier, not very succesful. I got one film course (The Child In Global Cinema), which was really good. The rest were also good, but just not film relevant. In the end I did get three courses what I needed for the number of ECTS points I had to have.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply as early as possible and get a good overview of the courses you want. And dont just apply to the university because of some very specific courses. It should also be the city and the experience that is interesting to you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I will say the level was a bit lower sometimes (for the sociology course anyway)  My two other courses were a nice level and   The assignments and exams were fine. I will say, it would have been nice to get more help for change students on writing, cause they do it differently. And off course you dont know what is specifically required of you

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I liked the lecturers and the smaller seminar groups. Though the level is a bit lower than in CPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: The Child in Global Cinema, Digital Art and Gender, sexuality and culture

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely The Child in Global Cinema!! - such a good lecture and class. Also Digital Art, if you are interested in art and the digital world.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Trips are definitely really nice to go on and I went more than I expected. It's good to have saved some money for that.

It's hard to make a generalisation of money that I spent pr. month, because some months I used a lot more money on trips and food (like the spring break) and others I didn't use that much.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Off course I didn't use much money on food cause it was catered. But living in UK is just a bit more expensive than you imagine. Like train tickets for trips or other stuff. Especially when you cant work on the side.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Trips, societies and sports!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely the trips and yoga. They have a lot of free sports like yoga, pilates, spinning and so on. Really nice to try out.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Ireland, Scotland and hikes like Peak District or Lake District. Also other towns or cities in England like York, London, Liverpool and so on!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was fine because of the English language. Thought off course there were a lot of differences, but thats the interesting thing.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Definitely be open to asking people in your classes to see each other after class. Also go to events like sports, trips and 
Also get a catered hall if possible, cause it's so much easier to meet exchange students this way. Also the Nordic society is a great way to meet nordic people!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Definitely the young English people in halls not cleaning up after themselves...

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really liked how open people were and it's easy to talk to new people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Remember that this is not your normal life. Off course you're gonna be spending more time alone and its not the same, but embrace it! Go on solo trips and explore even if you're alone.
2. Remember that all the other exchange students are also far away from home or alone. And people want to be social!
3. There are so many things to try or do. It's great to say yes and try new things. Just also remember to take care of yourself and take breaks.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Explore the city! Go to Northern Quarter, Ancoats, Fletcher Moss Gardens, Gay Village! Try different pubs and cafes and restaurants. It's so nice to be able to know this new city and walk around. Go out into the nightlike ( I recommend Blues Kitchen with live music)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Just being able to live in a new country for almost five months and making new friends!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I had some family emergency and had to go home. But other than that it can be hard to be alone or feel lonely sometimes.  Though its all a part of the experience!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
